title: Flavor Q1: The `C3` Reference Cone Does Not Force the Trace
verdict_rationale: Issue: The statement that every C3-invariant state is scalar on the singlet and doublet blocks is false for complex 3-by-3 density matrices; the cyclic shift has three one-dimensional complex eigenspaces and permits unequal weights on the two nontrivial characters. Why this blocks: The runner tests one admissible state but never computes the full commutant, so its four PASS results do not establish the stated two-block cone, although the explicit counterexample to trace selection and the rho-free Q algebra remain valid. Repair target: Add and justify a real/CPT/conjugation constraint and recompute the exact commutant, or weaken the note to the explicit-counterexample statement. Claim boundary until fixed: The displayed rho_(1:1) proves stipulated C3 covariance alone does not force the trace, but the two-block cone characterization is not established.
